name: Chevrolet Corvette C4 ZR-1
description:
The Chevrolet Corvette ZR-1, debuting in 1989, represents the ultimate expression of the C4 generation Corvette. Nicknamed the 'King of the Hill', the ZR-1 was General Motors' ambitious project to create the world's fastest production sports car by combining American muscle with European engineering sophistication.

Following GM's acquisition of Lotus in 1986, the British engineering firm was tasked with developing a revolutionary new engine and chassis improvements. The result was the LT5, an all-aluminum 5.7-liter V8 featuring dual overhead camshafts per bank (32 valves total), designed and built by Mercury Marine. This sophisticated powerplant initially produced 375 horsepower, later increased to 405 horsepower in 1993 with improved cylinder heads, exhaust system, and valvetrain.

The ZR-1 featured a wider rear body to accommodate massive 315mm rear tires, revised suspension tuning developed by Lotus, upgraded brakes, and a unique convex rear fascia with rectangular taillights. The advanced FX3 selective ride control system offered driver-adjustable damping.

With 6,939 examples produced between 1989 and 1995, the ZR-1 was significantly more expensive than the standard C4 Corvette, but offered genuine supercar performance with a top speed exceeding 180 mph and world-class handling dynamics. It remains one of the most technologically advanced and collectible Corvettes ever built.
author: IFSO
